knowledge_point.title: Solving First-Order Initial Value Problems Using Integrating Factors

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following initial value problem.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\left(1\right)y=2,\quad y(0)=-1
$$

Select the correct options below.

An integrating factor for this equation is $I(x)=$ {{field-1}}.

The solution to the initial value problem is $y(x)=$ {{field-2}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
This equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x),
$$

with $P(x)=1$ and $Q(x)=2.$

We compute an integrating factor using the definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & =e^{\int P(x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & =e^{\int 1\,\text{d}x} \\  & =e^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation in standard form by $I(x)=e^{x}$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}e^{x}\cdot (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+1y) & =e^{x}\cdot 2 \\ e^{x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+e^{x}y & =2 e^{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{x}) & =2 e^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{x})\,\text{d}x & =\int 2 e^{x}\,\text{d}x \\ ye^{x} & =2\left(1 e^{x}\right)+C \\ ye^{x} & =2 e^{x}+C \\ y & =\left(C + 2 e^{x}\right) e^{- x}\end{aligned}
$$

This is the general solution. To find the value of $C$ corresponding to the specific solution, we apply the initial condition $y(0)=-1$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0) & =\frac{(2 e^{(0)})+C}{(e^{(0)})} \\ -1 & =\frac{2+C}{1} \\ C & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=2 - 3 e^{- x}.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & =e^{\int P(x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & =e^{\int 2\,\text{d}x} \\  & =e^{2 x}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}e^{2 x}\cdot (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2y) & =e^{2 x}\cdot 4 \\ e^{2 x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2 e^{2 x}y & =4 e^{2 x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{2 x}) & =4 e^{2 x}.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{2 x})\,\text{d}x & =\int 4 e^{2 x}\,\text{d}x \\ ye^{2 x} & =4\left(\frac{1}{2} e^{2 x}\right)+C \\ ye^{2 x} & =2 e^{2 x}+C \\ y & =\left(C + 2 e^{2 x}\right) e^{- 2 x}\end{aligned}
$$

This is the general solution. To find the value of $C$ corresponding to the specific solution, we apply the initial condition $y(0)=-1$ as follows:

$$

$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=2 - 3 e^{- 2 x}.
$$
